## Tour with a trek to Laguna Esmeralda from Ushuaia

Not far from [Ushuaia](/argentina/place/ushuaia/), among Tierra del Fuego's mountains, lies [Laguna Esmeralda](/argentina/place/laguna-esmeralda/). Its waters often take on a turquoise hue, while subantarctic forest, peat-filled valleys, and rocky slopes surround its shores. The lagoon can be reached along a natural trail that begins outside the city.

Our separate [Laguna Esmeralda trek](/argentina/ushuaia/laguna-esmeralda-hike-from-ushuaia/) is linked to the **[13-day "Incredible Argentina: Buenos Aires, Ushuaia, El Calafate and Iguazu" tour](/multi-country/tour/incredible-argentina-patagonia/)**. This is an active excursion, distinct from a sightseeing visit to Tierra del Fuego National Park or a boat trip along the Beagle Channel.

## The hiking route

After leaving Ushuaia on National Route 3, the walking section begins. The trail crosses subantarctic forest, peatlands, and streams. Along the way, hikers may see signs of beaver activity, including dams across small rivers.

The hike to the lagoon takes **approximately 2 hours each way**. There is a stop by the water with a packed lunch and a hot drink before travelers return along the same path. The outing therefore takes more time and effort than a short stroll near the city harbor.

| Stage | What to expect |
|---|---|
| Departure from Ushuaia | Drive to the trailhead |
| Hiking section | Forest, peat bogs, and streams |
| Lagoon | Stop, snack, and hot drink |
| Return | The same nature trail |

The standalone excursion includes **a packed lunch and a hot drink**. Prices start at $105. Other transport arrangements, group conditions, and language options should be confirmed for the chosen date. Do not assume that the trail will be dry or equally accessible in every season.

## How the trek fits into the 13-day journey

The ["Incredible Argentina" tour](/multi-country/tour/incredible-argentina-patagonia/) takes in Buenos Aires, Ushuaia, El Calafate, and Iguazu Falls in that order. Ushuaia features on day 3, after a flight from Buenos Aires. A standalone excursion module to Laguna Esmeralda is listed alongside this part of the itinerary.

**The trek is described as an optional activity.** Its appearance among the related excursions means that the outing may be arranged, not that it is guaranteed to be included in the price of the main tour. Given the hiking time, flight arrival time, and weather, the trekking day must be planned separately.

The next section of the journey includes [Tierra del Fuego National Park](/argentina/place/tierra-del-fuego-national-park/) and the Beagle Channel. These offer different experiences: scenic sightseeing with short stops and a maritime excursion. Laguna Esmeralda requires a substantial walk over natural terrain.

## How the lagoon differs from other Tierra del Fuego routes

Around Ushuaia, you can choose boat tours, road trips, and treks. What makes Laguna Esmeralda special is that the main natural attraction is reached on foot across several kinds of landscape. Forest gives way to open peat bogs and then a valley where the brightly colored lagoon lies between mountains.

Argentina's national tourism portal describes this as one of Tierra del Fuego's popular hiking excursions, crossing forests and wet ground. Conditions change considerably with the season: waterlogged soil, snow, and ice may make walking more difficult.

If your priority is seeing birds and sea lions, a cruise on the Beagle Channel serves a different purpose. If forest, peatlands, and a mountain lagoon appeal to you, the [Esmeralda hike](/argentina/ushuaia/laguna-esmeralda-hike-from-ushuaia/) can become the main active experience of your time in Ushuaia.

## Preparation and safety on the trail

You will need waterproof hiking boots with non-slip soles, warm layers, and protection from wind and rain. Carrying water and an extra snack is helpful even when a packed lunch is provided. Weather changes rapidly in this region, and particular care is needed on boggy sections after rain and during the colder months.

Before arranging the outing, confirm the trail's difficulty and actual condition, group size, guiding arrangements, transfer times, and whether a replacement program is possible in bad weather. For an optional activity scheduled between flights, sufficient free time is especially important: the transfer to the trailhead, hike, and return drive take up a substantial portion of the day.

## Frequently asked questions about tours to Laguna Esmeralda

### How long is the walk to the lagoon?

According to the [excursion description from Ushuaia](/argentina/ushuaia/laguna-esmeralda-hike-from-ushuaia/), it takes about 2 hours each way, returning along the same route.

### Is the trek included in the main tour price?

It is listed as an optional activity. Arrangements and the additional price must be agreed for the specific [13-day itinerary](/multi-country/tour/incredible-argentina-patagonia/).

### Is food provided on the trail?

Yes. The standalone excursion description includes a packed lunch and a hot drink.

### Is this a driving excursion?

No. After the transfer to the trailhead, the route is on foot through forest and peat bogs. Appropriate footwear and preparation for Tierra del Fuego weather are essential.

## Boat excursion from Ushuaia to Martillo Island

From [Ushuaia](/argentina/place/ushuaia/), you can sail along the Beagle Channel to Martillo Island, known for its penguin colonies. This **separately charged boat excursion** includes a transfer to the port of approximately **20 minutes**, followed by about **2 hours of navigation**.

These figures describe two stages of the route, not the total stated duration from departure at the hotel to the return. Boarding, operational stops, and the drive back depend on the specific program.

## Penguins and seabirds of the Beagle Channel

Martillo Island draws visitors mainly for its seasonal colony of **Magellanic penguins**. **Gentoo penguins** are also found here. The Beagle Channel area is home to birds of open water and rocky shores, including cormorants, albatrosses, petrels, and terns.

Wildlife sightings do not follow a timetable. Bird numbers, viewing distances, and the species encountered on any particular day depend on the season, weather, and animal behavior. The crew is responsible for safe vessel maneuvers and maintaining the appropriate distance from shore.

In addition to the colony itself, travelers enjoy views of the channel and the mountainous shores of Tierra del Fuego. This distinguishes a maritime outing from a short visit ashore, where most of the time is spent beside penguins rather than on the water.

## Can you land on the island?

**Landing on Martillo Island is not confirmed for this boat excursion.** The regional tourism authority distinguishes between viewing wildlife from a vessel and authorized walking visits to the colony.

If going ashore is important, compare the [guided group walk among penguins](/argentina/ushuaia/ushuaia-walking-with-penguins/) and confirm the exact route for your date. Do not choose one service based on photographs of another or assume that any vessel is permitted to land passengers.

The two excursions also have different terms: the group walking option costs **$350 per person** and has an English-speaking guide, while the boat excursion to Martillo is **charged separately**, with no fixed amount specified here.

## Penguin season and preparing for the voyage

According to Ushuaia's tourism authority, the penguin-viewing season on Martillo generally runs from **October to April**. However, sailings depend on wind and sea conditions. When planning several days in Ushuaia, it is sensible to allow flexibility to reschedule the maritime outing.

Bring a windproof, waterproof jacket, warm layers, a hat, and shoes with non-slip soles for the deck. Protect your camera or phone from sea spray. If you are prone to seasickness, ask in advance about the vessel's characteristics and discuss personal medical advice with a doctor.

For other itineraries focused on wildlife, see [wildlife journeys](/interests/wildlife/).

## Frequently asked questions about the Martillo Island boat trip

### How long is the boat portion?

This excursion specifies **approximately 2 hours of navigation**, plus about **20 minutes for the transfer to the port**. These should not be added together and presented as the program's full duration.

### Can visitors walk among the penguins?

Landing is **not confirmed under the terms** of this boat trip. Visiting the colony on foot requires a separate authorized format.

### Which penguins might you see?

In season, the island is visited by **Magellanic and gentoo penguins**. Sightings of either species depend on natural conditions.

### Is this excursion included in the main tour price?

No. It is an **optional excursion requiring separate payment**. No specific price is stated here.

### What happens in strong winds?

The operator decides whether sailing is possible according to actual conditions. Plan for a possible change of time or date rather than assuming navigation is guaranteed in all weather.

## Tours featuring the Martillo Island penguin boat excursion

The [boat trip to the penguins of Martillo Island](/argentina/ushuaia/martillo-island-penguin-boat-trip/) departs from [Ushuaia](/argentina/place/ushuaia/) and crosses the Beagle Channel toward the colony on [Martillo Island](/argentina/place/martillo-island/). It is a standalone excursion that can be added to a longer journey around Argentina and Patagonia. The excursion specifies a transfer to the port of about 20 minutes and approximately 2 hours of navigation.

**An important condition: the excursion is charged separately.** Its inclusion as a module in the description of a longer tour does not mean the ticket is already included in the trip price. Below we compare only Ada Tours itineraries linked to this excursion.

## Which itineraries feature the boat trip?

**[Argentina Deluxe in 11 days](/multi-country/tour/luxury-argentina-buenos-aires-patagonia-iguazu-11-days-2026-2027/)** combines Buenos Aires, El Calafate, Ushuaia, and Iguazu. The penguin boat excursion appears as a separate block after a day in Tierra del Fuego National Park and before travel from Ushuaia toward Iguazu. It has its own terms, so check whether a boat outing can be added to the main days rather than assuming it is included automatically.

| Itinerary | Distinctive feature |
|---|---|
| Deluxe, 11 days | Ushuaia between glaciers and Iguazu |
| Patagonia, 14 days | Optional island outing for $450 |

In both cases, the multi-day journey covers much more than penguins: other cities, glaciers, flights, and natural areas occupy part of the schedule. If Martillo Island is the main goal, set aside dedicated time for the boat excursion from Ushuaia and confirm availability aboard the vessel.

## Boat excursion versus walking on the island

This excursion includes **navigation to the colony**. It should not be interpreted as a guaranteed landing or walk among the birds. Different operators provide separate formats: boat viewing from the deck, a maritime program with a ground transfer to the embarkation point, or an island walk under special rules.

For example, the [14-day "Best of Argentina" tour](/multi-country/tour/best-of-argentina-14-days/) lists a separate penguin-walking module with a **different canonical ID**. That does not establish that this particular boat excursion is included. When comparing tours, distinguish wildlife viewing from the water from going ashore, the time needed to reach the island, departure locations, and prices.

## When can you see the penguins?

Martillo Island's season follows the penguins' breeding cycle and time spent on the island. Ushuaia's tourism authority describes maritime viewing mainly **from October through March–April**. Magellanic penguins are more common, and gentoo penguins are also present. The first birds may return in late September, but that does not mean a visible colony is available to tourists on every date.

The presence of penguins, a suitable weather window, and the departure of the vessel cannot be guaranteed based on the calendar month alone. When planning, check the excursion's current operation for specific dates, restrictions on visiting the colony, and options for rescheduling in high winds. Weather changes quickly on the Beagle Channel, and a windproof jacket and warm clothing are needed on the open deck even on a relatively mild day.

## How to fit a boat excursion into the itinerary

Martillo Island can be combined with other excursions from Ushuaia, but each activity needs its own time allocation. [Tierra del Fuego National Park](/argentina/place/tierra-del-fuego-national-park/) is explored through forest trails and bays, whereas the maritime excursion depends on the boat schedule and passage by water. A land-based outing does not replace navigation to the colony.

Before booking, check whether the tour provides enough nights in Ushuaia, how tightly the next flight is scheduled, and where the boat section begins. Two excursion modules appearing close together in a description do not guarantee both can take place on the same day without additional arrangements.

If penguins are not your principal objective, compare [tours in Argentina](/argentina/tour/) covering more natural regions. If penguins are the main draw, choose a trip with a realistic amount of time in Ushuaia and a confirmed separate boat booking.

## Frequently asked questions about tours featuring Martillo Island

### Is the penguin boat trip included in the tour price?

The excursion page clearly states that it is charged separately. A specific 14-day itinerary mentions $450 per person; the terms of the other tour must be confirmed from its offer.

### Can you land on the island?

The product described here is a boat excursion. The ability to go ashore depends on a different excursion format and cannot be inferred from the words "penguin trip."

### When should you plan a viewing trip?

The colony season, generally October to March–April, is usually suitable for maritime excursions. Actual bird presence and vessel operation depend on wildlife and weather.

### Can you combine the island with the national park?

Yes, these are two different possible activities from Ushuaia. Their timetables, additional costs, and return times must be coordinated within the selected multi-day tour.

## Tierra del Fuego National Park: group excursion from Ushuaia

Near [Ushuaia](/argentina/place/ushuaia/), the Andes meet the sea, and forests and lakes give way to the coast of the Beagle Channel. Here lies [Tierra del Fuego National Park](/argentina/place/tierra-del-fuego-national-park/), one of Argentine Tierra del Fuego's foremost natural attractions.

We offer a **group excursion with an English-speaking guide**. Its itinerary connects several contrasting parts of the park: the Pipo River, Ensenada Zaratiegui Bay, Lake Roca, and Lapataia Bay. The program offers an introduction to the region's nature without the need to select a long hiking route in advance.

## Why this park differs from northern Patagonia

The national park protects southern forests, mountain valleys, peat bogs, glacial lakes, and a maritime coastline. It is an unusual combination: wooded slopes descend almost to the water, and mountains remain visible between the tree trunks.

Argentina's official tourism portal notes that the park has marked hiking trails of varying difficulty and areas where visitors can observe characteristic local birds. Signs of beaver activity are also present, having changed some streams and forested valleys.

This environment is particularly rewarding for travelers who have already seen Patagonia's glaciers and want to discover the wetter, more wooded far south. Tierra del Fuego weather is changeable, with wind, rain, and sudden drops in temperature possible near the water and in open areas.

## The Pipo River and Ensenada Zaratiegui Bay

The first part of the route introduces the landscapes around the **Pipo River**, whose valley runs between wooded mountain slopes. The road near Mount Susana shows the topography that makes [Ushuaia](/argentina/place/ushuaia/) seem squeezed between sea and mountains.

The itinerary then passes through **Ensenada Zaratiegui Bay**. Here, the contrast between forest, cold seawater, and surrounding peaks is especially vivid. On suitable days, Redonda Island is visible from this area.

These stops are confirmed in the excursion description. However, the exact walking times and the sequence of stops are not specified in the listing; they depend on the group's actual route and access conditions.

## Lake Roca and Lapataia Bay

Another significant stop is [Lake Roca, also called Acigami](/argentina/place/lago-roca/). Mountains and forests surround its shores, while the weather changes the color of the water and the visibility of distant slopes. The lake offers tranquil views after the marine coastline and reveals the mountainous interior of the national park.

[Lapataia Bay](/argentina/place/lapataia-bay/) is part of the Beagle Channel coast and is known as an area reached by National Route 3. Here, visitors encounter wetlands, forest, low mountains, and the striking geography of Argentina's far south.

Our itinerary also includes lagoons, a beaver dam, and a forest cabin. These are elements of the program, but their precise visiting order does not guarantee that every natural stop will be accessible in all weather.

## Group sightseeing versus an independent hike

The national park offers many hiking routes. However, **Ada Tours' excursion is a group introduction to several landscapes**, not a promise of a lengthy trek along a difficult mountain trail.

| Format | Main interest |
|---|---|
| Group sightseeing excursion | Several natural environments |
| Long-distance trek | Walking effort and the trail |

A sightseeing trip is convenient for those who want to see varied terrain in one outing. If your priority is a long hike, its distance, difficulty, and guiding arrangements need to be agreed as a separate activity.

**The duration and separate price of our excursion have not yet been specified.** The format is group-based and the guide speaks English. The structured lists of included and excluded services are empty, so park entry tickets, meals, and hotel transfers cannot be described as paid for without confirmation.

## How to prepare for your trip

Take windproof and waterproof outerwear, closed shoes, and water. Tierra del Fuego can be cool even during the Southern Hemisphere's summer. It is particularly important to stay on permitted trails and follow signs in forested and coastal areas.

When visiting from Ushuaia, arrange the group's meeting point and return time in advance so you can continue exploring the city at a relaxed pace afterward. If wildlife viewing is also on your plans, consider the separate [Martillo Island penguin walk](/argentina/martillo-island/martillo-penguin-walk/). It is a different product, and its transport and price are not automatically part of the national park visit.

## Frequently asked questions about Tierra del Fuego National Park

### Is the excursion conducted in Russian?

This program provides **guiding in English**. A Russian-speaking guide is not confirmed for this group excursion.

### Which places are on the route?

The Pipo River, Ensenada Zaratiegui, [Lake Acigami](/argentina/place/lago-roca/), and [Lapataia Bay](/argentina/place/lapataia-bay/), as well as other natural areas of the park.

### Are park admission tickets included?

The excursion listing does not confirm which entrance tickets have been paid for. The conditions should be clarified for the specific booking.

### Is the trip suitable for someone without trekking experience?

It is described as a group sightseeing program with stops at natural attractions, not a specialized long-distance hike. Confirm the specific walking sections and requirements in advance.

## Tours featuring an excursion to Tierra del Fuego National Park

The [group excursion with an English-speaking guide](/argentina/ushuaia/tierra-del-fuego-english-group/) departs from [Ushuaia](/argentina/place/ushuaia/) for [Tierra del Fuego National Park](/argentina/place/tierra-del-fuego-national-park/), where forests and mountain valleys reach bays along the Beagle Channel. Our excursion route covers the Pipo River, Ensenada Zaratiegui Bay, Lake Roca (Acigami), and Lapataia Bay.

This is an **English-language group excursion**. It should be distinguished from other standalone Tierra del Fuego tours and from a full day of trekking: several stops are specified, but there is no promise of a demanding, multi-kilometer trail.

## Which multi-day tour includes this excursion?

This excursion is directly linked to the ["Best of Argentina: 14 days with Bariloche and Iguazu" itinerary](/multi-country/tour/best-of-argentina-14-days/). On day 7, after arrival in Ushuaia, the group visits the park with an English-speaking guide. The day includes a view of Redonda Island, the [Pipo River](/argentina/place/pipo-river/), [Ensenada Zaratiegui Bay](/argentina/place/ensenada-zaratiegui/), [Lake Roca](/argentina/place/lago-roca/), and [Lapataia Bay](/argentina/place/lapataia-bay/).

The same tour separately offers an **optional penguin excursion to Martillo Island for $450 per person**. It is a different standalone module. The appearance of both activities within one day does not mean the maritime excursion is included in the paid national park visit.

The main 14-day route covers far more than this single day: Buenos Aires, Perito Moreno Glacier, Ushuaia, Bariloche, and Iguazu. Choose the trip first for its overall combination of regions and length, then consider optional activities in Ushuaia.

## Which places are covered in the park?

**[The Pipo River](/argentina/place/pipo-river/)** and its surrounding forests reveal Tierra del Fuego's valleys. **[Ensenada Zaratiegui](/argentina/place/ensenada-zaratiegui/)** reaches the coast and offers views of a bay backed by mountains. **[Lake Roca (Acigami)](/argentina/place/lago-roca/)** is part of the park's lake district. **[Lapataia](/argentina/place/lapataia-bay/)** represents the southern bays and coastal viewpoints.

| Place | Main attraction |
|---|---|
| Pipo River | Forest and river valley |
| Ensenada | Seaside bay |
| Lake Roca | Lake beneath mountains |
| Lapataia | Coast and boardwalks |

The source excursion also mentions Mount Susana, Redonda Island, lagoons, a beaver dam, and a forest cabin. The time spent at each location and the final sequence depend on the program and road conditions. This list should not be taken as several independent, lengthy excursions: these are stops on one outing.

## How the excursion relates to the season and physical effort

Even in summer, Tierra del Fuego can have chilly winds, rain, and sudden changes in conditions along the open coastline. Dress in layers: a waterproof, windproof jacket, comfortable shoes, and protection from dampness. Specialized mountain equipment is not automatically required for the main sightseeing tour through the listed stops.

**Some walking trails in the park have seasonal restrictions.** Argentine authorities note that certain trails operate mainly from November to April. If participants want to add a challenging trek to the group excursion, it is a separate activity requiring confirmation of the particular trail's accessibility and the time available.

Travelers should also consider park entry schedules, transport arrangements, and possible restrictions on access to particular coastal areas. In the colder season, visiting standard viewpoints and undertaking a long independent hike should not be regarded as interchangeable.

## How the national park differs from Ushuaia's maritime excursions

The park showcases Tierra del Fuego's forests, rivers, and lakes. A [boat trip to Martillo's penguins](/argentina/ushuaia/martillo-island-penguin-boat-trip/) depends on navigation along the Beagle Channel and the colony's seasonal presence. It is another product with separate logistics and payment. If both activities matter, allocate time in advance instead of assuming there will be an unplanned free evening.

For a broader choice of multi-day journeys in the region, see the [Argentina tours catalog](/argentina/tour/). Compare the number of nights in Ushuaia, the guide's language, included excursions, and the onward flight.

## Frequently asked questions about tours featuring Tierra del Fuego

### Is there an English-speaking guide?

Yes. The standalone excursion has a group format with guiding in English. Day 7 of the linked 14-day tour also specifies an English-speaking guide.

### Which places are included on the route?

The Pipo River, Ensenada Zaratiegui Bay, Lake Roca, and Lapataia Bay, as well as the scenic and nature stops identified in the itinerary.

### Is Martillo Island's penguin colony included?

No. It is listed separately as an optional excursion on the linked tour, with a price of $450 per person. It is not part of the standard national park itinerary.

### Can you hike the longer trails independently?

That depends on the trail, season, path conditions, and time available. The group sightseeing excursion does not itself include a confirmed extended trek.
